headline: GOLD HOLDS $4,724 AS US-IRAN PEACE HOPES EASE INFLATION FEARS; silver surges 7% on the week
snippet: Gold pulled back $15 to $4,724/oz on May 8 but held near all-time highs as optimism over a US-Iran peace deal triggered falling oil prices and eased prolonged-inflation fears. Silver topped $80/oz for the first time since mid-March, locking in a 7%+ weekly gain — the metal is up more than $49/oz year-over-year.

headline: COPPER NEAR $6.23/LB: China acid export ban strips 3M tonnes from seaborne supply as AI buildout roars
snippet: Copper surged to $6.23/lb (+1.62% on May 8, +35% YoY) as China's ban on sulphuric acid exports — a critical input in copper refining — removes an estimated 3 million tonnes from the seaborne market through at least December, squeezing major importers Chile, Indonesia, and India. The supply shock arrives simultaneously with sustained AI infrastructure and power grid spending driving structural demand.

headline: COT REPORT MAY 8: How speculators are positioned in gold, silver, and the USDX ahead of Iran talks
snippet: GoldSeek's weekly Commitment of Traders breakdown for May 8 dissects speculative and commercial positioning in gold, silver, and the US Dollar Index. Essential reading for junior mining investors tracking institutional money flows at a moment when geopolitical catalysts — an Iran deal, China tariffs — can move metals sharply in either direction.

headline: CHINA IMPORTED 790+ TONNES OF SILVER IN EARLY 2026 — solar manufacturing demand shows no sign of slowing
snippet: GoldSeek's Gold SWOT analysis flags China's outsized early-2026 silver import surge — 790+ tonnes — overwhelmingly driven by solar panel manufacturing, which underpins the structural demand case for silver even as the metal digests its run above $80/oz. Prince Silver also reported standout drill results of 7.62 metres grading 230 g/t silver.

headline: ANALYST: Gold stock weakness is M&A bait — producers piling up cash at $4,800+ realized gold prices
snippet: Kitco's John Feneck argues the persistent lag between gold equities and the bullion price will force cash-rich producers into M&A, citing Agnico Eagle's record Q1 2026 operating margins — AISC of $1,483/oz against a $4,861/oz realized gold price — as evidence of the capital flood waiting to be deployed into undervalued junior names.

headline: MOTLEY FOOL: 2 mining stocks to buy in May — one posting record operating margins
snippet: Motley Fool names two miners as May buys, anchored by Agnico Eagle's widening AISC-to-gold-price spread and SSR Mining's earnings momentum following an 84% revenue surge in Q1 2026. Both companies benefit from operational leverage to gold at multi-year highs without the balance sheet risk of smaller explorers.

headline: SSR MINING +20%: Q1 EPS nearly triples as $4,770 realized gold price turbocharges revenue
snippet: SSR Mining posted Q1 2026 EPS of $1.15 — nearly three times the year-ago figure — on 84% revenue growth, powered by a realized gold price of $4,770/oz versus $2,935/oz a year earlier, sending the stock up 20% in a single session on May 6. The result illustrates how leveraged mid-tier producers are to the current gold price environment.

headline: HIGH GRADE: Collective Mining hits new gold at Apollo Ramp Zone in Colombia — 14 rigs running by Q2
snippet: Collective Mining (TSX: CNL) delivered high-grade gold hits in maiden Ramp Zone holes at the Apollo system in Caldas, Colombia, confirming western extension and depth continuity. The company is scaling to 14 drill rigs before end of Q2 2026, backed by US$135M in cash — one of the better-funded juniors in the current cycle.

headline: QUEBEC GOLD: Opus One hits 8.22 g/t Au over 8.5m in Abitibi greenstone winter drill program
snippet: Opus One Gold Corp (TSX-V: OOR) returned its best hole yet at Noyell in Quebec's Abitibi greenstone belt: Hole NO-26-07 graded 8.22 g/t Au over 8.5m true width (7.16m), including a bonanza subzone of 49.1 g/t Au over 1.34m. Additional results are pending as drilling continues on the northern portion of the property.

headline: MINING DEALS HIT $21.6B — strongest Q1 since 2023 as critical minerals security drives consolidation
snippet: Global mining M&A hit $21.6B across 121 transactions in Q1 2026, the strongest start to a year since 2023, as supply-chain security concerns push institutional capital toward critical mineral assets. US projects captured 48% of January funding and Canadian assets 18%, with strategic partnerships replacing mega-mergers as the dominant deal structure.

headline: ATHABASCA BASIN: Standard Uranium advances Davidson River drill program as Rocas delivers new targets
snippet: Standard Uranium (TSX-V: STND) is advancing its 2026 drill campaign at Davidson River in Saskatchewan's southwest Athabasca Basin after the Rocas geophysics program identified priority targets across the Warrior, Bronco, and Thunderbird conductor corridors — one of the world's most prolific uranium exploration addresses.

headline: RARE EARTH ROUND-UP: Key deals and supply chain moves in the week of May 4-9, 2026
snippet: Rare Earth Exchanges' weekly deals summary covers the standout transactions and strategic moves May 4-9, as governments accelerate sovereign financing to build ex-China separation and refining capacity — the competitive frontier now moving beyond mining into metallization, magnet manufacturing, and state-backed offtake frameworks.
